commonFaq.a: No. A request is the brief our team works from. We find an operator and a ride for your date, then send a written quote. Nothing is booked until the quote is accepted, payment is completed and an operator has committed.

commonFaq.q: Who sets up and runs the ride?
commonFaq.a: Rides are delivered, set up and operated by the carnival operator we arrange for your event. We coordinate the details with you and with them.

commonFaq.q: How much space and power does a ride need?
commonFaq.a: It depends on the ride and the operator's equipment. Tell us about your site in the request — surface, available space, access and power — and we confirm what fits before quoting.

Some cities, counties and venues require permits or approvals for amusement rides. Requirements vary by location, so check with your venue and local authority; we can tell you what the operator will need from the site.

groups.name: Birthdays
planningNotes: Tell us the guests' ages so we can suggest rides that suit them.
Backyards often have limited access for trucks and trailers — note gates, slopes and overhead wires in your request.
Book early for weekend dates in peak season.

groups.name: Religious & cultural celebrations
planningNotes: Let us know the schedule of the day (ceremony, meal, dancing) so the ride runs when guests are free to use it.
Venues such as banquet halls and places of worship may have rules about outdoor equipment — check before requesting.
Tell us the guests' age mix; many of these events include young children and grandparents.

groups.name: Family milestones & parties
planningNotes: Describe the site: lawn, driveway, parking lot or venue grounds.
Tell us the expected number of guests and their ages.
If the venue is rented, ask the venue manager about ride rules before requesting.

planningNotes: Schools and districts often require paperwork from vendors — ask your administration what they need.

groups.name: Colleges & universities
planningNotes: Campus events often go through student activities and risk management — start that approval early.
